title: The innovation of the potter’s wheel: a comparative perspective between Mesopotamia and the southern Levant
lineage: Publisher-formatted original case study of excavated ceramics. Shares Baldi and part of the Tell Feres assemblage with the 2021 study.

passages.locator: The potter’s wheel in northern Mesopotamia: a view from Tell Feres al-Sharqi; Fig. 2
passages.note: A late Ubaid workshop, about 4700 BCE, had a small clay disc with a slight socket, compatible with a pivot. Evidence of rotational energy used during wheel-coiling begins later in levels 5–4B and 4A, about 3900–3800 BCE.
Early southern Levant wheel-coiling predates the northern Mesopotamian finds. Neither independent innovation nor diffusion from the southern Levant is demonstrated.
